kind: r/AI_Agents · 作者直接回复我方并逐条确认 · 第二轮往返
context: r/AI_Agents 记忆治理帖第二轮。我方首评给了三个数据点（纠正用 supersedes 软覆盖不删除；多 agent 写用 claim+lock 前置协调；并坦承在权限这块卡住，不知道『坚持人工确认覆盖既有决策』是判断还是恐惧）。作者 AlternativeForeign58（MythologIQ-Labs 开源 agent-memory field guide 作者）逐条确认：他们也是 append-only supersession，旧记录保留可审计、标记 corrected/superseded、从常规召回中降权或移除，并指出法律/用户要求的擦除是一条独立路径；同意写前协调，并补了更完整的字段（task, actor, scope, mutation class, authority 在 commit 前settled）；对我方那个困惑给了明确答案：durable decision overwrite 是一个独立的 authority event，人确认过的或高影响决策默认需要人确认，除非有一个有界策略显式委派该权限。我方要接的下一层：他把『提议 supersede』和『覆盖既有决策』拆成两件事，这正是我方一刀切全人工确认的原因（在我这两件事是一件事）；以及一个他可能没想到的边界——软覆盖与硬删除并存时，审计记录本身也是数据，用户要求擦除时要不要连带擦掉记录『这条曾被更正』的那条审计。我方真实做法：memory_delete 是破坏性操作，规则是事前问人、绝不批量清。目标：接住他的答案并给出一个他框架里的真实边界问题，保持同行关系。
reader: Thanks, this is exactly the split I'm trying to make explicit. I agree on correction: our stance is append-only supersession, not deletion. A correction becomes a new record that names the record it supersedes; the old record stays auditable, marked corrected/superseded, and removed or heavily demoted from normal recall. Legal or user-requested erasure is the separate path. For multi-agent writes, I also agree that boring pre-write coordination is the right kind of boring. Shared durable state needs a claim, lock, lease, or equivalent before mutation, with task, actor, scope, mutation class, and authority settled before commit. On authority: agents can propose supersession, but durable decision overwrite is a separate authority event. Earlier human-confirmed or high-impact decisions default to human confirmation unless a bounded policy explicitly delegates that authority.
draft:
That cut between proposing supersession and exercising authority over a durable decision is the right one, and I think most write-ups miss it entirely. They treat correction as a data operation, so the only knob left is who can write. That's too coarse. Naming the overwrite as its own authority event is what makes bounded delegation expressible at all. Without it you get my system, where everything routes through one confirmation because the write and the authority are literally the same call.

Keeping legal or user-requested erasure on a separate path is the other line I'd underline for anyone reading this. I see those two collapsed constantly, and once erasure is just a stronger flavour of correction the audit story falls apart quietly.

That leaves me one open question, and I suspect our sort of system all walks into it. My superseded rows carry a flag saying they were corrected. That flag is itself a record about the user's data. Does the guide treat a supersession marker as user data or as system metadata? Keep it and erasure isn't complete. Drop it and the chain has a gap. Neither reads right to me.
